title: Al-Mughni, the Enricher
tomorrow: rain cancels round two of the paint day. bad luck, or harm held back?

cards: A raise that's spent before it lands. A new phone, and then the next new phone. Enough has a way of moving, like the horizon when you walk toward it.
Yesterday's question: why does one verse put rich and content side by side? It's in Surah an-Najm, in a list of things God does, and it's a strange little pair.
Two verbs, one breath, as if getting more and having enough were two halves of the same gift.

teach.b: In Pickthall's words, it is He "Who enricheth and contenteth." Today's Name is Al-Mughni, the Enricher. So why pair the two?
Here's the solution, from a hadith the Prophet, peace be upon him, gave in plain words: richness isn't having a lot of things; real richness is richness of the soul.
The Arabic phrase is ghina an-nafs, the self that has enough. That's the piece to tell a friend tonight: in this hadith, rich isn't a bank balance. It's a state of the soul.
And it explains the verse. Riches without contentment never arrive; the horizon keeps moving. Contentment without anything at all is a different struggle.
So Al-Mughni gives both: sometimes more, and sometimes the richer gift, the sense of enough. Notice this doesn't make asking wrong.
The Prophet taught a prayer that asks for exactly this: suffice me with what is lawful instead of what is forbidden, and enrich me by Your bounty so that I need no one but You.
Asking for more, and asking for enough, in the same sentence. Just like the verse.

how: Muslims ask for sufficiency in the Prophet's words: suffice me with what is lawful instead of what is forbidden, and enrich me by Your bounty so I need none but You.

o: the Owner of the earth's treasures
the Rewarder, who pays for good deeds

games.q: more, and enough — tap the pairs.

s: in the hadith, real richness means having a lot of things
the Prophet said real richness is richness of the soul.
Pickthall's verse says He 'enricheth and contenteth' in one breath
being content means never asking God for more
the Prophet's own prayer asks: enrich me by Your bounty.

games.q: you finally buy the sneakers you saved for. two days later a friend shows up in the newer pair, and yours suddenly feel old. what does today's hadith point to?
o: save again; you'll feel rich once you own the newest pair.
richness is of the soul: your shoes didn't change, the comparison did.
get rid of them; owning nice things is the real problem here.
games.why: the hadith puts richness in the soul, not the shoe rack. the verse asks for more and for enough; it doesn't make owning things wrong.

practice: Rest both hands open on your knees, palms up, the posture of asking. If you pray, ask in your own heart for sufficiency, or use the Prophet's words: enrich me by Your bounty.
Otherwise, name one thing that is already enough today, and let your open hands hold it until the bell.

wordCard.voice: Al-Mughni. The Enricher, who gives riches, and gives the richer thing too: enough.

orig.note: Arabic: the Enricher, from the traditional list of the Names; 53:48 says He enriches and contents.

carryVoice: Hold this: he enriches, sometimes with more and sometimes with the feeling of enough. Fifteen sixty-three, done.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 6446; Sahih Muslim 1051 (richness is richness of the soul)
